sections.h2: What does the Forsyth County Register of Deeds record?
sections.html:
The office records and keeps the public land records for the county: deeds, deeds of trust and mortgages, satisfactions, plats, leases, notices of foreclosure and several other filings.

The county's recording page also lists assumed business names, rights of way, covenant agreements, UCC filings, affidavits, powers of attorney, separation and prenuptial agreements and living wills. Wills, divorces and estates are handled by the Clerk of Court, so an heir selling an inherited Forsyth County house files estate paperwork elsewhere and brings the deed here once authority is in place.

The Census Bureau counts 401,718 residents and 184,703 housing units in the county as of July 2025, and the 2020 to 2024 survey puts the owner-occupied rate at 63.6 percent with a median owner-occupied value of $250,400.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed in Forsyth County?
sections.html:
Bring or send the original signed instrument, or submit it electronically through an approved vendor, between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. on a business day.

  • In person: the document is returned to you at the counter once it is recorded.
  • By mail: send a business check, money order or cashier's check for the exact recording fee, payable to the Forsyth County Register of Deeds, with a self-addressed stamped envelope. Do not mail cash.
  • Electronic: the submitter signs an agreement with an authorized e-recording provider and completes a memorandum of understanding. E-files must arrive by 4:30 p.m. on a business day.

Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies, and priority follows the order of registration. That makes timing matter when two instruments touch the same parcel. The office is a recording office only, and staff cannot draft documents or give legal advice.

sections.h2: What are the Forsyth County recording fees?
sections.html:
A standard document costs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each added page, and a deed of trust costs $64 for the first 35 pages plus $4 per added page.

Real estate recording fees as printed on the Forsyth County Register of Deeds fee page
InstrumentFee printed
Standard document$26 first 15 pages, $4 each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 first 35 pages, $4 each added page
Plat$21 each sheet
Non-standard document$25
Satisfaction instrumentsNo fee
Multiple instruments as one$10 each plus the recording fee
Certified copy$5 first page, $2 each added page
Uncertified copy$.25 per page

The page adds $2.00 for each party listed over 20, including attachments and exhibits. The state sets these amounts in G.S. 161-10 and calls them complete and exclusive, so they match every other North Carolina county. Counter payments accept business checks, official bank checks, money orders and credit or debit cards, with a 3 percent card charge or a $1.00 minimum, and no card payments by telephone. Personal checks and e-checks are refused.

sections.h2: Who pays the transfer tax on a Forsyth County deed?
sections.html:
The seller, who is called the transferor in the statute, pays the excise tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

G.S. 105-228.30 sets the tax at one dollar on each $500 of the consideration or value, or fraction of $500. Half of the money goes to the county general fund and the other half is remitted to the Department of Revenue, with the county permitted to keep 2 percent of the state share. For a property that sits in more than one county, the tax is paid where the greater value lies.

The excise tax is separate from the property tax. County tax is billed to the owner of record on January 1, and the tax office suggests paying it at closing, so a seller should expect both items on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What format must a Forsyth County document meet?
sections.html:
Documents that miss the recording standard are charged an extra $25 as a non-standard document under G.S. 161-10.

  • Paper 8.5 by 11 inches or 8.5 by 14 inches, black type on white paper, single sided.
  • A blank margin of 3 inches at the top of the first page, side margins of at least half an inch, and type of 9 points or larger.
  • The type of instrument printed at the top of the first page below the margin.
  • Original signatures in the acknowledgment, or a certified copy of the original.
  • A deed shows the grantee's current mailing address, and a deed of trust prepared in North Carolina names the drafter on the front page.

These standards come from G.S. 161-14. Check a draft against this list before it leaves for the courthouse, since fixing a margin costs less than a surcharge.

sections.h2: How do I clear an old mortgage from the Forsyth County record?
sections.html:
The lender or noteholder cancels it by recording a satisfaction, and the office charges nothing to record one.

The county explains that a deed of trust or mortgage is a security instrument that is canceled once the debt is paid, while a deed is title and is never canceled. Cancellation is the responsibility of the owner or noteholder in the county where the instrument was recorded. The county lists several forms that can do the job: a satisfaction of security instrument, a trustee's satisfaction, a notice of satisfaction, a certificate of satisfaction and an affidavit of satisfaction.

Do not assume the lender has acted. The office states that payoff papers and satisfactions are not mailed to the borrower automatically after the loan is paid in full. A borrower can call the register of deeds to check that the loan is marked satisfied before ordering a copy of the record.

sections.h2: Where do tax maps and deed lookups fit in Forsyth County?
sections.html:
The tax office's parcel maps show lot lines, but the deed is the legal description to rely on.

The county's tax FAQ warns that parcel dimensions on tax maps are calculated for tax purposes only, and the acreage on a tax record may not match the deeded or platted acreage. To find legal lot dimensions, open the Deeds tab on the parcel's property detail page or use the register of deeds lookup. That is the practical step before a sale where a fence, a split lot or an old boundary dispute is in play.

sections.h2: What other services and fees does the Forsyth County office list?
sections.html:
Besides land records, the office charges for notary work and vital records, and it waives fees for some military papers.

  • Notary public: $10, and notarial acts are $5 for each signature, except when performed with an act that already carries a fee.
  • Comparing a copy for certification: $5.
  • Recording a military discharge and getting a copy: no fee, and the Thank a Veteran photo ID is also free.
  • Certified birth or death certificate: $10; marriage license: $60.

Heirs who need a certified death certificate pay $10 for it according to the fee page. Call the office to confirm which of these documents can be issued the same day.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Forsyth County?
faqs.a: A standard document is $26 for up to 15 pages with $4 for each additional page. The state sets these fees in G.S. 161-10, and a satisfaction of a deed of trust is free to record.

faqs.q: Does the Forsyth County Register of Deeds take personal checks?
faqs.a: No. The fee page says personal checks, counter checks and e-checks are not accepted. Business checks, official bank checks, money orders and credit or debit cards are.

faqs.q: When must an e-filed deed arrive in Forsyth County?
faqs.a: Electronic recordings must reach the office by 4:30 p.m. on a business day. In-person and mailed filings are handled during the 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekday hours.

faqs.q: Who pays North Carolina excise tax on a Forsyth County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. The rate is one dollar on each $500 of value or part of $500 under G.S. 105-228.30.

faqs.q: Can the register of deeds help me write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office records documents only, and state law bars staff from giving legal advice or telling you how to draft an instrument, so ask an attorney.
